root_cause.text: The IPv4 ICMP error delivery path in `net/ipv4/icmp.c` failed to special-case `IPPROTO_RAW`, so an incoming ICMP packet with an inner IP header protocol value of 255 could be incorrectly handed to a raw socket and trigger raw socket error handling/FNHE cache updates, despite `IPPROTO_RAW` being receive-disabled.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (protocol == IPPROTO_RAW) goto out;` in `icmp_socket_deliver()` and the commit message states that “a malicious incoming ICMP packet can set the protocol field to 255 and match this socket, leading to FNHE cache changes,” while `man 7 raw` says “Receiving of all IP protocols via IPPROTO_RAW is not possible using raw sockets.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The IPv4 ICMP error delivery path in `net/ipv4/icmp.c` failed to special-case `IPPROTO_RAW`, so an incoming ICMP packet with an inner IP header protocol value of 255 could be incorrectly handed to a raw socket and trigger raw socket error handling/FNHE cache updates, despite `IPPROTO_RAW` being receive-disabled.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (protocol == IPPROTO_RAW) goto out;` in `icmp_socket_deliver()` and the commit message states that “a malicious incoming ICMP packet can set the protocol field to 255 and match this socket, leading to FNHE cache changes,” while `man 7 raw` says “Receiving of all IP protocols via IPPROTO_RAW is not possible using raw sockets.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent ICMP delivery to IPPROTO_RAW sockets while preserving input error accounting for invalid packets.
intent_record.what: The function `icmp_socket_deliver()` was changed to replace an immediate error return on `pskb_may_pull()` failure with a `goto out` path, add a new early exit when `protocol == IPPROTO_RAW`, insert an explicit `return` after the normal delivery path, and add a new `out:` label that increments `ICMP_MIB_INERRORS` before exiting.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packets that cannot be fully pulled still count as ICMP input errors, but the error accounting is now shared with a new rejection path for `IPPROTO_RAW` sockets, which are prevented from receiving any ICMP delivery at all. Normal protocols continue to invoke `raw_icmp_error()` and any registered protocol error handler unchanged.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early exit in icmpv6_notify() for IPPROTO_RAW packets and assign a generic drop reason.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added in icmpv6_notify() after the existing drop-reason check: if nexthdr equals IPPROTO_RAW, the function now sets reason to SKB_DROP_REASON_NOT_SPECIFIED and immediately jumps to out. A brief comment was added above this new block.
intent_record.how: At runtime, packets whose next header is IPPROTO_RAW will now exit this path early with an explicit drop reason instead of continuing into the later packet parsing logic. This prevents further processing for that case and records a generic drop reason.

grouping_result.intent: Add an early exit in icmpv6_notify() for IPPROTO_RAW packets and assign a generic drop reason.

consistency_review.core_intent: Prevent ICMP delivery to IPPROTO_RAW sockets while preserving input error accounting for invalid packets.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the root cause by preventing ICMP error delivery to IPPROTO_RAW sockets, including an early exit for IPPROTO_RAW handling. This matches the vulnerability where ICMP packets with inner protocol 255 were incorrectly delivered to raw sockets.

candidates.rationale: This directly delivers ICMP errors to the protocol-specific raw socket path without excluding IPPROTO_RAW, which is the root cause described: an inner IP protocol value of 255 could be treated as a valid raw socket target and update raw-socket error handling/FNHE state.

This protocol lookup feeds the subsequent err_handler invocation for whatever inner protocol number is present, and without special-casing IPPROTO_RAW it allows protocol 255 to participate in ICMP error delivery.
This condition enables protocol-specific error handling for the looked-up protocol, which is problematic when the protocol is IPPROTO_RAW and should not receive ICMP errors.
This is the actual callback that can trigger raw socket error handling on protocol 255, embodying the incorrect delivery path described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This directly invokes the ICMP error handling path for the inner protocol without excluding IPPROTO_RAW, allowing protocol 255 to be treated as a valid raw-socket target and trigger raw socket error handling/FNHE updates.
This performs the protocol lookup used for ICMP error delivery, and without a special-case for IPPROTO_RAW it allows protocol 255 to proceed into protocol-specific error handling.
This condition gates delivery into the protocol-specific error handler, which is unsafe for IPPROTO_RAW because that protocol is receive-disabled and should not receive ICMP errors.
This is the actual callback that dispatches the ICMP error to the protocol handler, enabling incorrect raw-socket error handling for inner protocol 255.

    ipv4: Pull icmp socket delivery out into a helper function.

diff --git a/net/ipv4/icmp.c b/net/ipv4/icmp.c
index 4a049449305f..18e39d1895d4 100644
--- a/net/ipv4/icmp.c
+++ b/net/ipv4/icmp.c
@@ -634,18 +634,31 @@ out:;
 EXPORT_SYMBOL(icmp_send);
 
 
+static void icmp_socket_deliver(struct sk_buff *
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the ICMP error delivery path still unconditionally uses the inner header protocol to notify raw sockets and protocol err handlers. In the new helper, it does `int protocol = iph->protocol;`, then immediately calls `raw_icmp_error(skb, protocol, info);` and looks up `inet_protos[protocol]` with no special-case for `IPPROTO_RAW` (255). This is exactly the vulnerable construct described: an incoming ICMP packet with inner protocol 255 can be handed to raw socket error handling / FNHE updates. There is no check such as `if (protocol == IPPROTO_RAW) return;` or other receive-disable handling, so the fix is not present in this commit.

Author: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

    inet: Sanitize inet{,6} protocol demux.
    
    Don't pretend that inet_protos[] and inet6_protos[] are hashes, thay
    are just a straight arrays.  Remove all unnecessary hash masking.
    
    Document MAX_INET_PROTOS.
    
    Use RAW_HTABLE_SIZE when appropriate.
    
    Reported-by: Ben Hutchings <bhutchings@solarflare.com>
    Signed-off-by: David S.
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body includes the ICMP unreachable error delivery path and the protocol demux, so the relevant logic is visible. In the old code, the protocol was hashed with `hash = protocol & (MAX_INET_PROTOS - 1);` and then used as `inet_protos[hash]`, which could alias protocol 255 (`IPPROTO_RAW`) onto another protocol bucket. The patched code changes this to `ipprot = rcu_dereference(inet_protos[protocol]);`, i.e. direct array indexing with the real protocol number, which is the sanitize/fix for the demux issue. Because the snippet already reflects the corrected handling and no longer contains the vulnerable hash-masking construct, `has_bug` is false and `is_fixed` is true.
